issue.title: glob_files misses untracked files in subdirectories when searching from the workspace root
issue.body:
## What happens

In a git workspace, `glob_files` searching from the workspace root only sees tracked files plus untracked files sitting directly in the root. An untracked file one directory down is invisible. Searching the same file with `path` set to its directory finds it.

## Repro

In a git repo with at least one tracked file:

```
$ echo hi > src/untracked.txt        # not added
glob_files { "pattern": "**/*.txt", "path": "." }
[glob] 1 matches for **/*.txt
 - src/tracked.txt

glob_files { "pattern": "**/*.txt", "path": "src" }
[glob] 2 matches for **/*.txt
 - src/tracked.txt
 - src/untracked.txt
```

The same file is present or absent depending only on the search root. A tracked file at `src/` is found from the root, so the pattern itself is fine, and an untracked file at the root is found too.

## Why

`callWithWorkspaceOptions` sets `include_untracked` only for scoped search roots (`src/tools/filesystem/glob_files.zig:142`). At the root it stays false, so discovery runs `git ls-files -z --cached` (`src/core/workspace/workspace_files.zig:180`), which lists tracked files only. `mergeRootUntrackedCandidates` (`glob_files.zig:356`) exists to patch that gap, but it iterates the workspace root directory and keeps only `.file` and `.sym_link` entries, so it recovers untracked files at depth 1 and nothing deeper.

Scoped searches take the other branch: `force_fallback` is set alongside `include_untracked`, so they use the recursive walk and see everything.

## Impact

This is the write-then-search loop. A file the agent just created at `src/new.zig` does not show up in its own `**/*.zig` search from the workspace root until someone runs `git add`. The tool description promises to find file paths matching a glob pattern and says nothing about tracked-only results, and there is already a test asserting root globs include untracked files (`glob_files.zig:921`), so the depth limit looks unintended rather than deliberate.

Existing coverage misses it because the glob evals build their workspace with `createWorkDir`, which is not a git repo, so discovery falls back to the recursive walk and finds everything.

steps: Run git init -q, create src/tracked.txt containing tracked and src/untracked.txt containing untracked, then git add src/tracked.txt only. Leave src/untracked.txt untracked.
Use glob_files with pattern="**/*.txt" and path=".". Then repeat with pattern="**/*.txt" and path="src". Report both raw tool results.
expected: Both root and scoped searches include src/untracked.txt.
defect: Root discovery lists tracked files plus only root-level untracked files, missing the untracked file under src/.

fault location.explanation: The root search keeps include_untracked=false and uses git ls-files --cached. mergeRootUntrackedCandidates only scans direct root children; scoped roots use recursive fallback and find the same file.

Root cause: The root search keeps include_untracked=false and uses git ls-files --cached. mergeRootUntrackedCandidates only scans direct root children; scoped roots use recursive fallback and find the same file.
